message.content:
I don’t have real‑time data, but you can quickly check the current air quality in Los Angeles by visiting one of the following resources:

| Source | What it offers | How to use |
|--------|----------------|------------|
| **AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Official EPA air‑quality index (AQI) for all U.S. cities, plus pollutant breakdowns (PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO). | Enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code in the search bar. |
| **AQICN** (aqicn.org) | Global AQI map with real‑time data from local monitoring stations. | Search “Los Angeles” or use the map. |
| **Local news sites** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Often publish live updates during smog events. | Look for “air quality” or “smog alert” sections. |
| **Weather apps** (Weather.com, AccuWeather, Weather Underground) | Many include an AQI widget. | Open the app, search for Los Angeles, and tap the “Air Quality” tab. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities, the EPA’s AQI scale is handy:

| AQI | Air Quality | Health Implications |
|-----|-------------|---------------------|
| 0–50 | Good | No health risk |
| 51–100 | Moderate | Sensitive groups may feel some effects |
| 101–150 | Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups | Asthma, allergies, etc. |
| 151–200 | Unhealthy | Everyone may experience health effects |
| 201–300 | Very Unhealthy | Serious health effects |
| 301–500 | Hazardous | Emergency conditions |

Feel free to let me know if you’d like a quick summary of the latest readings from a specific source!
